subject: Aligning ownership lanes & tie-breakers for MSA / DPA / order form close
messages:
From: Anne Lopez <anne.lopez@medsight.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@medsight.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP and a couple of tie-breaker questions for legal sequencing

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move from eval to pilot. I attached our draft MAP (MAP_v1_shared.xlsx) that combines the procurement milestones with the technical evaluation checkpoints. Before I push this to our internal procurement track I have two quick tie-breaker questions where we need clarity from Redwood legal/ops: 

1) Data residency fallback: if we can’t land our preferred EU-hosted deployment, do we have a supported option for a dedicated tenant in us-east with contractual SLOs on data isolation, or is that only available under Private?
2) Order form acceptance: we want a short clause that ties the initial pilot order form to the MSA/DPA so we avoid duplicate signature paths — can Redwood confirm the preferred linking text (so our procurement can route correctly)?

If possible, could you share who on your side will own each lane (legal redlines, procurement sequencing, and technical acceptance)? That will help us accelerate internal handoffs.

Anne
Anne Lopez
Head of Procurement, MediSight AI
Attachments: MAP_v1_shared.xlsx
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anne Lopez <anne.lopez@medsight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and a couple of tie-breaker questions for legal sequencing

Thanks Anne — appreciate the clear MAP. I attached a short redline of the MSA (MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) and a one-page ownership lane summary below. I’ll summarize answers inline and propose a pragmatic close cadence.

Quick answers: 
- Data residency fallback: For pilot customers who cannot be on customer-managed Private right away, Redwood can offer a dedicated tenant in a shared-hosted region (us-east) with contractual isolation guarantees and audit logs. This is supported under a Dedicated+ commitment (we can include the wording in the DPA).
- Order form linking: We recommend the following linking clause: "This Order Form is governed by the Master Services Agreement (MSA) between the parties dated [date]. In the event of conflict, the MSA controls." Legal prefers that we capture the full MSA reference (name, date, and signature block) rather than an open-ended reference.

Proposed ownership lanes (who owns what):
- Legal redlines / contract language: Marissa Cole (Legal, redlines + sign-off)
- Procurement sequencing / commercial terms: Laura Bennett (Revenue ops / contracts)
- Technical acceptance / pilot runbook: Mateo Alvarez (solutions + onboarding)

Suggested close timeline (slim / aggressive): 3 weeks from redline lock to DocuSign if we can move in parallel:
Week 0: Redlines consolidated + MAP final 
Week 1: Legal approval + procurement routing 
Week 2: DocuSign + PO issuance + tech kickoff

Action items: 
- Marissa: I’m sharing the redline for your review (attached).
- Anne: Can you confirm that procurement can accept the linking clause above? Also please confirm the desired pilot region (EU preference noted).

– Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_v3_redlines.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and a couple of tie-breaker questions for legal sequencing

Thanks Mateo — I reviewed the attached redlines and have three notes to keep the close predictable: 

1) Risky clause: The customer requested a very strict data deletion SLA tied to monthly backups. We can accept a deletion commitment but must scope it to customer-managed keys or Dedicated deployments. For hosted shared-tenants we need carve-outs (we cannot certify deletion of backups that are shared infrastructure). Recommend the fallback language: "Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to delete customer data from active systems; backups are subject to standard retention and recovery processes unless Dedicated or Private deployment is in effect."

2) Linking text: The linking clause Mateo suggested is fine. I will draft a short paragraph that references the DPA by date and add a sentence that the Order Form is conditioned on execution of the MSA. That will satisfy procurement teams that want a single signature path.

3) Ownership/tie-breaker process: For any disputed items during redline consolidation we propose a two-step tie-breaker: (a) commercial vs legal ownership — if it is commercial (price/term) Laura will decide; if legal (warranty/liability) Marissa will decide. For cross-cutting items (e.g., data residency impacting price), we escalate to Karthik (VP Sales Ops) to adjudicate within 48 hours.

I can own the redline consolidation meeting next Wed at 10am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite. If that timing doesn’t work for Anne’s procurement team we can shift.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Anne Lopez <anne.lopez@medsight.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@medsight.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and a couple of tie-breaker questions for legal sequencing

Hi Marissa / Mateo — this is helpful, thanks. A couple quick confirmations from us: 

• We can accept the proposed linking clause and will mirror the MSA/date in the Order Form — Procurement confirms that will streamline routing.
• For data residency: our preference remains EU; second choice is Dedicated in ap-southeast for latency reasons, third is the documented dedicated tenant in us-east with contractual isolation (your described fallback). Procurement will flag the region preference in the PO.

On timing: Wed 10am PT for the redline consolidation works for my team — please send the invite. On DocuSign we typically require a two-business-day approval window from our legal once redlines are locked; can Redwood commit to sending a DocuSign package within 24 hours of lock?

Thanks,
Anne
